原文: Adeleida
译文: 阿黛莱达

原文: Hulph's Henchman
译文: 胡尔夫的爪牙

原文: Christoffer de Malamert
译文: 克里斯托弗·德·马拉梅特

原文: In the orcish caverns deep under the Moonshine Mountains. It was wielded by your magic twin, summoned by heretics to make you suspicious of heresy.
译文: 在月光山脉深处的兽人洞穴中。它曾被你的魔法分身所持有，异端们召唤她，为的是让你蒙上异端的嫌疑。

原文: God be with you, son. And God bless you for your generosity...
译文: 愿上帝与你同在，孩子。愿上帝因你的慷慨而赐福于你……

原文: Enough talking, demon. Soon, the wrath of God shall be upon you! You shall be cast back to hellish sufferings in no time!
译文: 说够了，恶魔。神的怒火很快就会降临到你头上！你马上就会被打回地狱的苦难之中！

原文: Of course, noble lord. What would you like to know? I have a feeling that we were having a conversation about really important things, but I just can't remember, what was it...
译文: 当然，贵族大人。您想知道什么？我总觉得我们方才在谈论极其重要的事情，可我怎么也想不起来，那是什么来着……

原文: First of all, good man, tell me, who you are?
译文: 首先，好人，告诉我，你究竟是谁？

原文: But then one of the girls managed to escape. She told the paladins about all the perversities the Duke committed. No need to go into details; guess you can imagine what he was doing to them. The paladins didn't hesitate and chased down the Duke who meanwhile tried to escape and brought him back to the city in chains. His execution was quite a show, people came from far and wide to see it. But the Duke seemed to be in quite a good mood, he was laughing madly all the time and just before he perished he uttered a terrible curse.
译文: 但后来其中一个女孩设法逃脱了。她把公爵犯下的种种变态行径都告诉了圣骑士。不必细说；想必你能想象他对她们做了什么。圣骑士们毫不犹豫地追捕了公爵——他当时正试图逃跑——并用铁链将他押回城中。他的处决场面颇为壮观，人们从四面八方赶来观看。但公爵的心情似乎相当不错，他一直在疯狂大笑，临死前还发出了一句可怕的诅咒。

原文: But of course, Father! My husband told me in the morning that we have a nice day today, so this is a beautiful day. My husband is a very wise man, you know.
译文: 当然可以，神父！我丈夫早上就告诉我今天天气很好，所以这是个美好的日子。我丈夫是个很有智慧的人，您知道的。

原文: Well, in fact, I did see something. It was an awful night. It was snowing heavily and I was looking around for some place to hide myself. When I passed by the tavern, I spotted someone climbing out of the window where the guestrooms are located. I quickly hid myself not to let him see me—it's never good to catch someone doing something wrong and let him see you, after all.
译文: 嗯，事实上，我确实看到了些东西。那是个可怕的夜晚。大雪纷飞，我正在四处寻找藏身之所。当我经过那家酒馆时，瞥见有人正从客房所在的那扇窗户爬出来。我赶紧躲了起来，没让他发现我——毕竟，撞见别人干坏事还被对方看见，总归不是什么好事。

原文: God has nothing to do with that, knight—it's probably Satan who had a hand in what happened after. That is, the Baron's spirit stayed imprisoned in the family mansion that became a real house of terror and everybody started to avoid it. Of course, tales about inexhaustible riches hidden in the dungeons under the Blutenreich mansion appeared soon, but nobody of those who decided to go there was ever seen again. Terrible laughter can be heard from that house in the dead of night, as well as laments of women and of children. I'm sure you can imagine what probably takes place there...
译文: 这事与上帝无关，骑士——后来发生的事，多半有撒旦在其中插手。也就是说，男爵的灵魂被困在了家族宅邸之中，那座宅邸成了一座名副其实的恐怖之屋，人人都开始避而远之。当然，很快就流传起布卢滕里希宅邸下方地牢里藏着无穷珍宝的传闻，可凡是决定前往那里的人，再没有一个被人见过回来。夜半时分，那座宅邸里会传出骇人的笑声，还有女人与孩童的哀哭。我相信你能想象那里大概在发生些什么……

原文: I promised to get some healing potions for one wounded werewolf, sir Knight.
译文: 我答应过要为一只受伤的狼人弄些治疗药水，骑士阁下。

原文: I'm sorry, but I have no time to search for your companion. I have an important mission.
译文: 抱歉，我没有时间去找你的同伴。我有重要的任务在身。

原文: Really? In that case we now look in the face of a man who detests nothing, because as the First Prophet said—ever so little a sin is like a murder. We face the man who doesn't detest to decry a remembrance of the deceased by destroying their graves, disturbing the peace of the dead and by stealing the belongings of their consecrated bodies. How monstrous! How foul! How depraved! Nevertheless I have to ask the prosecutor if he has any other proof supporting the charge. Do you have any other evidence on which basis we might find the defendant Vick Length guilty?
译文: 当真？如此说来，我们面前站着的是一个毫无敬畏之心的人，因为正如第一先知所言——再小的罪也如同谋杀。我们面对的这个人，肆意毁坏坟墓以亵渎对死者的纪念，惊扰亡者的安宁，并偷窃其圣化肉身的遗物，却毫无悔意。何其骇人！何其污秽！何其堕落！尽管如此，我仍须问公诉人是否还有其他支持指控的证据。你是否还有其他证据，可据以判定被告维克·伦斯有罪？

原文: All right, I'll take care of it. Juhasz Gotherr will be caught.
译文: 好吧，我会处理这件事的。尤哈什·戈特尔一定会被抓获。

原文: I won't risk my life in vain. My mission does not consist of killing hellspawns but of prosecuting their human henchmen!
译文: 我不会白白拿生命冒险。我的使命不是诛杀地狱造物，而是追捕它们的人类爪牙！

原文: Thank you, son.
译文: 谢谢你，孩子。

原文: Hello, son. I heard you were looking into the case of missing Bishop Quentinus. I'm glad you're still convicted you can help him. How is your investigation going on?
译文: 你好，孩子。我听说你正在调查失踪的昆提努斯主教一案。我很高兴你仍坚信自己能够帮助他。调查进展如何？

原文: Get out of here, noble lord. You're not welcome anymore.
译文: 滚出去，贵族大人。这里已经不欢迎你了。

原文: What?! The prosecution doesn't have the corpus delicti that serves as an evidence of guilt?! In that case come back later when you collect both parts of the dagger. Until then I suspend this pleading.
译文: 什么？！控方没有作为罪证的物证？！那样的话，等你收集齐匕首的两部分再回来吧。在此之前，本庭中止此次陈述。

原文: Really? I'm very sorry about that, my son. In that case you'll have to be put away as the time is ticking away and I really need to finish the ritual. Moreover I have a surprise for you. It's your companion Hugo de Montesque. He's one of my people. I'm sure you won't be surprised if he's going to join me!
译文: 是吗？我深感遗憾，我的孩子。既然如此，你便只能被除掉了——时间不等人，我还得完成仪式。此外，我还有一个惊喜要告诉你。那就是你的同伴，雨果·德·蒙特斯克。他是我的人。如果他加入我，我相信你不会感到意外！

原文: I beseech you, Your Holiness, please, give me the book.
译文: 我恳求您，阁下，请把那本书给我。

原文: Because he had a book we needed for the preparation of the summoning ritual. I killed him to cover all the tracks. Nobody was to know what book we gained from him. And beyond that, the fool wanted to extort me! He said that the Inquisition would be surely interested in what books I was interested. He wanted my body; he wanted to fornicate with me. But I didn't grant him that pleasure. I killed him.
译文: 因为他手里有一本我们准备召唤仪式时需要的书。我杀了他，是为了抹去一切痕迹——绝不能让任何人知道我们从他那里得到了什么书。更何况，那个蠢货还想敲扎我！他说宗教裁判所一定会对我在看什么书很感兴趣。他想要我的身体；他想与我交媾。但我没有给他这份乐趣。我杀了他。

原文: You poor wretch! You're toiling here with all those petty charges of yours and don't understand you stand against something that exceeds human comprehension. Stop pretending at being a brave knight of God and admit that even now you're looking into the face of eternal despair. You'll suffer for laying your hands on me. On me, the first concubine of Lord Baphomet! Oh yes, you've heard well! I fornicated with the Fallen Angel himself! He fertilized me with the seed of madness and made me the mother of his cursed children of Chaos. Come to me, my children! Your mother calls you! Kill that disgusting minion of the dead god! Eat his entrails and gouge out his eyes! Tear him to pieces and take me back to your father, Lord Baphomet!
译文: 你这可怜的虫豸！你带着那一桩桩卑琐的指控在此徒劳折腾，却不知自己所对抗的，已远超人类所能理解。别再假装是什么上帝的英勇骑士了，承认吧——即便此刻，你的眼中也映着永恒的绝望。你敢对我动手，必将付出代价。对我，巴风特领主的第一妃妾！哦，是的，你没有听错！我与那堕落天使本人交合！他以疯狂的种籽令我受孕，使我成为他那些受诅的混沌之子的母亲。来吧，我的孩子们！你们的母亲在召唤你们！杀了这个死神的肮脏走狗！撕开他的脏腑，挖出他的双眼！将他碎尸万段，把我带回你们的父亲——巴风特领主身边！

原文: God will lead us to a total and inevitable victory over the hellspawns and their servants—no matter where they hide. Do you understand, sir?
译文: 神将引领我们取得对地狱造物及其仆从彻底而不可阻挡的胜利——无论他们藏身何处。你明白吗，先生？

原文: You made a good decision, Father. You'll see that my services will be of much greater use to you then the services of a person who violated his holy mission!
译文: 你做出了明智的决定，神父。您会发现，我的效劳对您的用处，远胜于一个背弃了神圣使命之人的服务！

原文: And do you think it's possible that the heretics could have summoned the Fallen Angel Arthamon?
译文: 您认为异端者有可能召唤了堕天使阿尔萨蒙吗？

原文: And what's the matter? Do you think that because I'm dead you don't have to express appropriate respect to me, you stupid villager? In that case you're mistaken—I'll teach you good manners! Yeeeeaaarghhhh!
译文: 那又怎样？你以为我死了，你就不必对我表示应有的敬意了吗，你这个愚蠢的村民？那你就大错特错了——我这就教你什么是规矩！咿——啊啊啊啊！

原文: As you wish, sir. I'm going to find out myself.
译文: 如您所愿，先生。我会亲自去查清楚。

原文: But of course, noble lord. I'll be happy to answer all your questions.
译文: 当然可以，贵族大人。我很乐意回答您的所有问题。

原文: What rumors? I haven't heard anything yet...
译文: 什么传闻？我还没听说……

原文: You lie! I found the prints of your boots around a robbed grave!
译文: 你在撒谎！我在一座被盗的墓穴周围发现了你的靴印！

原文: Yes, of course, knight. What do you need to know?
译文: 当然可以，骑士。你想知道什么？

原文: You're thinking of the black gown of a judge of the Holy Inquisition, my son? That does you credit. God wishes us Inquisitors to improve constantly in our holy mission that the Almighty has put on our shoulders in his divine wisdom. Then know that every prosecutor of the Holy Office may become an Inquisitorial Judge, if he solves an assigned case under the supervision of a Curial Inquisitor, and then passes an examination of canon law and of secular law.
译文: 你想的是神圣宗教裁判所法官的黑色法袍吗，我的孩子？这值得称赞。上帝希望我们这些审判官在全能者以其神圣智慧托付于我们肩上的神圣使命中不断精进。那么请知晓：圣务院的每一位检察官，只要在教廷审判官的监督下承办一桩交办的案件，并通过教会法与世俗法的考试，便可成为裁判法官。

原文: No, I'm certainly not. You're not gonna get me there. I don't have any visions of the end of the world, I don't scream prophecies from my sleep and I've even thrown away my crystal ball as it was only good for dusting. Anyway it was no mountain crystal—just glass...
译文: 不，当然不是。你别想套我的话。我没有什么世界末日的异象，不会在睡梦中喊出预言，我连水晶球都扔了，它只配用来掸灰。再说那也不是什么山晶——就是玻璃……

原文: Hmm... Why do you think the heretic you're looking for here in Hillbrandt is exactly Edmond d'Arvias?
译文: 嗯……你为何认为你在希尔布兰特寻找的异端正是埃德蒙·达尔维亚斯？

原文: Oh, really? Well, in that case... In that case I agree, noble lord. You're very kind to offer me your help. I know an excellent seamstress who makes the most beautiful dresses the world has ever seen. Her name is Baroness Helen von Hunth. We used to be friends when I lived in Glatzburg. Find her, please, and ask her to make a grand wedding dress for me—a wedding dress worthy of the sight of Grand Duke Heidrick.
译文: 哦，真的吗？既然这样……既然这样，我同意，贵族大人。您愿意伸出援手，真是太好了。我认识一位出色的裁缝，她做的裙子是世上最美的。她的名字是海伦·冯·洪特女男爵。我住在格拉茨堡的时候，我们曾是朋友。请您找到她，请她为我缝制一件盛大的婚纱——一件配得上海德里克大公目光的婚纱。

原文: Who's gonna lead us now, when the First Knight don Rodrigo de Velacor is dead? The royal army is without its supreme commander... and any army without command flees when it comes to the first charge...
译文: 第一骑士唐·罗德里戈·德·维拉科尔死了，谁来带领我们？王室军队没有了最高统帅……而一支没有指挥的军队，遇到第一次冲锋就会溃逃……

原文: It was nothing...
译文: 没什么……

原文: Knight, could I ask you to do me a favor? It's terribly important and you as God's knight really can help me!
译文: 骑士，我能请你帮个忙吗？此事万分要紧，而你作为上帝的骑士真的能帮我！

原文: What? Are you telling me, it means Natalia wasn't murdered?
译文: 什么？你是说，这意味着娜塔莉亚并非被谋杀？

原文: This is Edmond d'Arvias's letter to Bishop Trevorius in Glatzburg. It reads:\\n\\nDear friend,\\nI sincerely hope you receive this letter in kind health and fair circumstance, despite the evils plaguing us all. I would trouble you, Trevorius, to aid the bearer of this letter with an investigation of the utmost importance. Though I tremble to write the words which follow, I fear even more your disbelieving them, old friend. There has been a conspiracy in Hillbrandt to invoke the fallen angel, Arthamon—a conspiracy, I fear, which has likely succeeded. What makes the case all the more troubling is that Bishop Vallarian, who you know well from the Inquisitorial Curia of Glatzburg, has been convicted of the crime.\\nAs you can see, this is no petty case of hearsay heresy. Though the betrayal of an inquisitorial judge frightens me to no end, Trevorius, certain truths which have come to light bring a chill to my very soul. Though it may only be the rambling of a doomed man, Judge Vallarian left a warning for the bearer of this letter; the Children of the New Order, of which you certainly know more than I, walk the Earth again.\\nI would ask you to afford the bearer of this letter all possible assistance with his investigation, and to help him discover the truth behind Judge Vallarian’s betrayal. I fear more than my peace of mind hangs in the balance, old friend.\\nEver Yours, Edmond
译文:
这是埃德蒙·达尔维亚斯在格拉茨堡写下的致特雷维里乌斯主教的信。信上写道：

亲爱的朋友，
尽管邪恶正困扰着我们所有人，我仍由衷希望你收到此信时身心康健、境遇顺遂。我要劳烦你，特雷维里乌斯，协助持信人进行一项至关重要的调查。写下接下来这些字句时我双手颤抖，老朋友，但我更害怕的是你不肯相信。希尔布兰特发生了一起召唤堕落天使阿尔萨蒙的阴谋——我担心，这阴谋恐怕已经得逞。更令此案棘手的是，你在格拉茨堡宗教裁判庭便熟知的瓦拉里安主教，已被判定犯下此罪。
如你所见，这绝非一桩道听途说的异端小事。尽管一名宗教裁判法官的背叛已让我恐惧万分，特雷维里乌斯，某些浮出水面的真相更令我的灵魂发寒。纵然这可能只是一个将死之人的胡言乱语，瓦拉里安法官还是给持信人留下了一句警告：新秩序之子——关于他们你自然比我更清楚——已重临世间。
我恳请你给予持信人一切可能的协助，帮助他查明瓦拉里安法官背叛背后的真相。老朋友，悬于一线的，远不止我一人的安宁。
永远属于你的，埃德蒙

译文: 兽人钥匙

原文: A single glance at this abominable volume would likely drive a normal man insane. The book itself is bound in human flesh, and painted with scenes of the most unimaginable depravity. The scenes, painted in blood which never dries, swirl and slither across the book’s ghastly, writhing cover. If what I know of the book is true, it was written in the year 850 by the Dark Prophet, Lucius, founder of the Children of New Order. Judging from the living script, it seems to detail the rise of the fallen angels, Arthamon, Baphomet and Cerdie.\\n\\nLucius describes the rites for summoning the fallen angels in the most thorough... and sickening terms. His descriptions and instructions as to how the Children should go about committing the atrocities needed to bring Hell to Earth are terrifying, in a word. This Dark Prophet, this Lucius, could never have been a man of flesh and blood like me. The implications of that possibility are... are too frightening to even consider.\\n\\nLord protect me, there’s more. Apparently, one of the Children will be “Marked by the Beast,” and it will be his or her duty to perform the ritual necessary to bring Hell to our world:\\n\\n”Blessed are the chosen, the vessels of corruption! Carry on your person, marked champion, this tome, for through it are channeled the powers which will open the way. To open the gates of Hell, you must be willing to sacrifice. First, you must make an offering of the blood of your brow, breast, and loins. When the unclean blood has mixed at your feet, use it as ink to inscribe the drawn mark upon the gateway. Your mortal form will be consumed, for great and powerful are the fires of Hell, but your spirit will live forever among the princes of the damned, and your sacrifice will bring about the end of God’s feeble, flawed creation.”\\n\\nMay the angels forgive me for what I have read, and may God shed his mercy over me. I must end this, once and for all.
译文:
仅凭一瞥，这本可憎之书便足以令常人发疯。书本身以人类的皮肤装订，封面绘满了难以想象的堕落场景。那些场景用永不干涸的鲜血绘成，在书封可怖而蠕动的表面上盘旋滑行。若我所知属实，此书成于850年，作者是暗黑先知卢修斯——新秩序之子的创立者。从那些活生生的文字来看，书中详述了堕落天使阿尔萨蒙、巴弗灭与塞尔迪的崛起。

卢修斯以最详尽……也最令人作呕的笔触，描述了召唤堕落天使的仪式。他关于新秩序之子应如何犯下那些罪行、以将地狱带入人间的描述与指示，简而言之，令人胆寒。这位暗黑先知，这个卢修斯，绝不可能是像我这样的血肉之躯。那种可能性所隐含的意味……实在太可怕，甚至不敢去想。

主啊，护佑我，后面还有。据记载，新秩序之子中有一人将"被兽标记"，由他或她来履行仪式，将地狱带入我们的世界：

"蒙福的是被拣选者，腐化的器皿！背负这卷圣典吧，被标记的勇士，因为正是通过它，通往彼方的力量得以传导。欲开启地狱之门，你必须甘愿献祭。首先，你须以额间、胸前与腰腹之血作为祭品。当污秽之血在你脚下交融，便以它为墨，将画好的印记刻于门扉之上。你的肉身将被吞噬，因地狱之火强大而炽烈；但你的灵魂将与被诅咒的诸王永存，而你的牺牲将终结上帝那脆弱而残缺的造物。"

愿天使宽恕我所读到的一切，愿上帝将怜悯倾注于我。我必须终结这一切，一劳永逸。

原文: Directorium Inquisitorum, also known as the Golden Tome of the Defender of the Faith, was written between 241 and 250 by Ruphiel, a monk of Saint Marchiel Monastery in the Moonshine Mountains. Ruphiel, who belonged to the Order of Saint Orthenius, spent a great deal of time studying the life and deeds of the Patron, and penned this work as a guide for inquisitors and other defenders of the Faith.//n//nThe church claims that Ruphiel wrote the book under the influence of Divine Inspiration, and the text has become one of the cornerstones of the Inquisitorial office of the Papal Cathedral.\\n\\nThe text outlines the signs an inquisitor should be wary of when investigating the goings-on of heretics and the unclean. Things like twitching, unnatural movements, or an aversion to holy symbols... even the description of those imbued with unholy resistance to torture; the book contains everything a discerning inquisitor would ever need to know to root out and destroy any infestation of heretical belief.
译文: 《审判官指南》，又称《信仰捍卫者金典》，由月光山脉圣马切尔修道院的修士鲁菲耶尔于241至250年间写就。鲁菲耶尔隶属圣奥塞尼乌斯教团，曾以大量时光钻研主保圣人的生平与事迹，并写下此书，作为审判官及其他信仰捍卫者的指南。//n//n教会声称，鲁菲耶尔是在神启的感召下写成此书的，而这篇文本也已成为教廷大教堂审判官署的基石之一。\\n\\n文中列出了审判官在调查异端与不洁者行迹时应当警惕的种种征兆：抽搐、反常的动作，或是对圣物的厌恶……书中甚至描写了那些对刑罚怀有亵渎性抗力之人；此书囊括了一名敏锐的审判官为根除并摧毁异端信仰滋生蔓延所需知晓的一切。

原文: A backsword is a stabbing weapon with a long, straight blade. Together with sabers, the backsword is one of the principal weapons of cavalrymen, especially heavy cavalry.\\n\\n The average backsword is a little heavier than a saber and is crafted specifically for stabbing. One of the cavalry commanders of King Jonathann III, the renowned Grand Duke Horst van den Brecht, was quoted as saying that the only true weapons were stabbing weapons – other blades and blunts were the weapons of cowards. That particular commander trained his heavy cavalry in the art of backsword fighting to the exclusion of fighting with spears or standard swords. Despite the prevalence of bows on the battlefield, the backsword is still the favored weapon of cavalry charges looking to inspire fear.
译文: 单刃直剑是一种以长而笔直的剑刃刺击的武器。与军刀一道，单刃直剑是骑兵——尤其是重骑兵——的主要武器之一。\\n\\n 一把普通的单刃直剑略重于军刀，专为刺击而锻造。乔纳森三世国王麾下的骑兵指挥官之一、著名的大公霍斯特·范登·布雷希特曾言：唯有刺击武器方为真正的武器——其他刀刃与钝器皆为懦夫所用。这位指挥官训练重骑兵时，只练单刃直剑刺击之术，完全摒弃长矛与常规刀剑。尽管弓箭在战场上愈发普遍，单刃直剑仍是骑兵冲锋时用以激起恐惧的首选武器。
